/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 22 July 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 2715 (45)
Baltic Capesize Index: 4114 (184)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2120 (-61)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1715 (-15)
Baltic Handysize Index: 905 (2)
CAPESIZE
The market extended its recovery today, with improving sentiment evident across both the Pacific and Atlantic basins as stronger demand and a tightening supply picture continued to underpin rates. The BCI 182 5TC gained a further $1,668, closing at $37,308. The C5 index advanced by 0.605 to $11.775, while the C3 route posted a much stronger gain, rising $1.145 to $33.445, reflecting the continued improvement in the South Atlantic. In the Pacific, sentiment continued to strengthen despite only one major miner being active. Operator-controlled cargoes and an increase in coal business helped offset the limited miner presence, with the regional tonnage list also appearing slightly tighter. The C5 bid improved to around $11.50, while owners were now seeking in excess of $12.00. There was market talk of $11.80 having been concluded, although details remained unconfirmed. The sole miner in the market was understood to be resisting prevailing levels and had yet to conclude any business at the time of writing. The Atlantic also maintained its positive momentum. Conditions from South Brazil and West Africa into China continued to improve, supported by reports that one of the major miners declared several cargo nominations yesterday, sustaining healthy demand. Stronger fixtures concluded late yesterday carried through into today’s trading, with bids opening around $33.00 against offers near $33.75, while market discussion suggested business may have been concluded around $33.50 for slightly earlier than index dates.
PANAMAX
In the Atlantic, market sources commented that owners appeared increasingly inclined to secure employment today, while sentiment continued to soften. This has reportedly created near-term rate pressure for both trans Atlantic and fronthaul trades. However sources noted that although there has been an uptick in trans Atlantic fixing activity at lower levels, fresh cargo has emerged helping to replenish rather than add to the existing cargo book. Brokers also highlighted that some Charterers who had been more active in the Atlantic in recent days are now stepping back and re-evaluating their bids. Market participants stated that with Pacific market fundamentals still appearing weaker, many owners are favouring remaining in the Atlantic. This is superficially increasing the pool of available tonnage willing to trade in the basin. A similar trend has been observed on the P6 route, where owners with the flexibility to do so are choosing to ballast from the Far East. This is creating a surplus of available tonnage and subsequently reducing offer levels in an effort to stimulate bidding activity. The Pacific continued to soften today as tonnage availability increased further, while demand from both the North Pacific and Australia was reportedly insufficient to restore balance to the market. Messrs CSE were reported to have covered their 75,000/10 coal stem from East Australia to Kaosiung or Taichung for mid-August dates in the high $13.00’s. Overall, the P5TC fell $546 on the day, closing at $19,083.
SUPRAMAX
As midweek passed the North American routes tumbled further as a lack of fresh demand took hold, with an Ultramax reported for fronthaul grains below $30,000. The Continent was said to be stable without much being reported and the Mediterranean retained a firmer tone supported by the grain season. In the south sentiment is wobbling despite the lack of tonnage, as fresh demand is scarce, or being held back. In Asia the market appeared mixed and positional, although rates in general remain flat, with the South African market seeing the most activity and rates holding or slightly improved. The 11TC average saw its biggest decline for a few weeks and was down $189 to close at $21,674.

Atlantic

The Nordultra (61,614 2015) Port Everglades 25 July went on subjects basis delivery US Gulf for a trip WC South America intention grains at $31,000 with Oldendorff and the Feng Mao Hai (63,413 2017) was said to be on subjects delivery Houston 5-9 August for a trip intention petcoke to EC South America at $22,000 with Norden. Oldendorff were also linked with the Bordo Mavi (61,261 2021) open Philadelphia 25 July delivery US Gulf for a trip Far East intention grains at something around $28/29,000 on subjects, but exact details did not come to light.

Asia

The HTK Galaxy (61,400 2011) Dhamra 21 July went on subjects to Norden basis delivery passing Singapore for a trip via Indonesia to the Philippines intention coal at $20,000 and the Pindos (57,420 2016) Chittagong 23-26 July fixed via EC India redelivery China intention iron ore at something in the low $13,000’s with Auxin. Finally, Enesel put the Desert Pioneer (60,980 2022) Navlakhi 24-29 July on subjects for a trip via South Africa redelivery EC India at $19,500.
HANDYSIZE
The market saw mixed performance today, with sentiment largely shaped by positional factors. The BHSI gained 2 points to reach 905, while the 7TC average settled at $16,295. The trend from yesterday persisted across the Continent and Mediterranean, where limited fresh enquiry meant activity was subdued. In the US Gulf and South Atlantic more activity and fresh demand emerged, but this was insufficient to absorb the excess tonnage available, keeping rates under pressure and overall sentiment weak. Notable fixtures included the Yasa Magnolia (40,558 2025) being placed on subjects from Port Arthur with pellets at $21,000 by Ultra Bulk, and the Nisa Naree (39,000 2015) open Veracruz heard placed on subjects for an inter-Caribbean trip at just under $12,000 by ADM, although further details were not disclosed. Meanwhile Asia continued to gain momentum, with rates firming despite limited reported fixtures and little fresh information.

Vale Production Report

In Vale’s q2 production report, the company announced total iron ore production was up 14.6 Mt quarter-on-quarter at 84.3 Mt, the highest second quarter production since 2018. Northern System output rose 6.4 Mt from the first quarter to 39.6 Mt, including a 3.6 Mt increase in S11D production to 23.4 Mt. ai_analysis.summary: 2026年7月22日干散货市场走势分化，巴拿马型和超灵便型承压下行，好望角型延续反弹势头。BDI指数上涨45点至2715，好望角型领涨+184点至4114，但巴拿马型-61点至2120，超灵便型-15点至1715。虽有好望角型太平洋和大西洋市场同步走强的积极信号，但整体运力过剩与需求疲软令中小船型前景不明。

sections.title: Market Structure
sections.content: 好望角型市场延续反弹，C3大西洋航线劲扬$1.145至$33.445，太平洋C5站上$11.50。巴拿马型供需失衡加剧，太平洋运力堆积导致P5TC日跌$546至$19,083，船东被迫竞价揽货。超灵便型北美国际航线大幅回落，灵便型亚太航线逆势走强。整体而言，大船需求改善，小船基本面仍弱。

sections.title: Dry Bulk Signals
sections.content: C3航线：南非/巴西至中国需求旺盛，矿商大量提名货载，FFA远月维持Backwardation结构。P5TC：太平洋市场持续恶化，运力过剩倒逼租金下行，短期未见拐点。SMX 11TC：跌破$22,000整数关口，北美粮食出口旺季未能提振市场。Handysize：亚洲航线HS5/HS6涨幅居前，区域分化明显。

sections.title: Trading Focus
sections.content: 关注好望角型8月合约$32,250-33,250区间突破方向，矿商挺价意愿若持续或推动C3现货站上$34.00。巴拿马型远月合约Cal27跌至$16,250，估值偏低但缺乏抄底逻辑，建议观望。Supramax与Handysize关注太平洋煤炭及东南亚铝矾土货盘释放情况。
